(char 0-10707)\\n    - Troubleshoot nodes that can't reach Amazon S3 endpoints (char 922-3164)\\n    - Troubleshoot invalid token requests (char 3165-4815)\\n    - Troubleshoot instances that can't search for Windows updates (char 4816-8931)\\n    - Troubleshoot updates that fail to install (char 8932-10097)\\n    - Troubleshoot a missing patch (char 10098-10378)\\n    - Additional troubleshooting steps (char 10379-10707)\\n\\n# How do I troubleshoot patching issues related to Amazon EC2 Windows instances when I use the Patch Manager AWS-RunPatchBaseline document?\\n\\nI want to troubleshoot errors that I receive when I use the AWS-RunPatchBasline document to patch Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) Windows nodes.\\n\\n---\\n\\nShort description\\n-----------------\\n\\nThe following issues cause errors when you use the [AWS-RunPatchBaseline Systems Manager Command document (SSM document)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/patch-manager-aws-runpatchbaseline.html) for Patch Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager:\\n\\n*   Your Amazon EC2 instance or managed node can't reach Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) endpoints.\\n*   The token request isn't valid.\\n*   Your EC2 instance can't search for Windows Updates.\\n*   Updates fail to install after you download them.\\n*   A patch is missing.\\n\\nResolution\\n----------\\n\\n### Troubleshoot nodes that can't reach Amazon S3 endpoints\\n\\nThe following error messages show that the instance can't connect to the Amazon S3 endpoints.They also occur because the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) instance profile attached to your instance lacks the necessary permissions to connect to your endpoints:\\n\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : The underlying connection was closed: An unexpected error occurred on a send\\\"\\n*   \\\"An error occurred when executing PatchBaselineOperations: Unable to connect to the remote server\\\"\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : Access Denied\\\"\\n\\nTo resolve these errors, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Check that you attached the IAM permissions for the instance profile to the node. For the minimum permissions, see [AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) communications with AWS managed S3 buckets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/ssm-agent-technical-details.html#ssm-agent-minimum-s3-permissions).\\n2. Check that your instance profile has [permission to access the Quick Setup S3 bucket](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/quick-setup-patch-manager.html#patch-policy-s3-bucket-permissions).\\n3. If your profile lacks permission to access the Quick Setup S3 bucket, then [add the policy to your profile](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/quick-setup-patch-manager.html#patch-policy-bucket-permissions).\\n4. To check the connection to the endpoint, run the following command in PowerShell:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    tnc s3.example-region-id.amazonaws.com -port 443\\n    ```\\n    **Note:** Replace **example-region-id** with your AWS Region ID.\\n\\nIf you can't connect to the endpoint, then take one of the following actions:\\n\\n*   If the instance is in a public subnet, then check that the instance's **RouteTable** uses an internet gateway to route to the internet.\\n*   If the instance is in a private subnet, then use a NAT gateway to connect, or create [an S3 gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html#create-gateway-endpoint-s3), or [interface](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-interface-endpoint.html#create-interface-endpoint-aws) VPC endpoint.\\n\\n### Troubleshoot invalid token requests\\n\\nThe following example error messages show that SSM Agent uses incorrect credentials:\\n\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation failed with: The security token included in the request is invalid:\\\"\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation: Instance Id i-00fe5918abcdef12 doesn't match the credentials\\\"\\n\\nTo resolve these errors, [update SSM Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/ssm-agent-automatic-updates.html#ssm-agent-automatic-updates-console) to version 3.2.183.0 or later.\\n\\nTo use an earlier SSM Agent version, find the shared credentials, delete them, and then test the patch again. Shared credentials exist in your environment variables, your **SystemProfile** folder, or your User Profile.\\n\\nTo locate the credentials, press the **Windows key** and then enter **environment variables**. Check the **environment variables** window for variables named **AWS\\\\_ACCESS\\\\_KEY\\\\_ID** and **AWS\\\\_SECRET\\\\_ACCESS\\\\_KEY**. Then, locate and delete credentials that match your **AWS\\\\_ACCESS\\\\_KEY\\\\_ID** and **AWS\\\\_SECRET\\\\_ACCESS\\\\_KEY** variables at the following locations:\\n\\n**Note:** It's a best practice to create a backup of the following folders before you delete shared credentials that they contain.\\n\\nFor your SystemProfile folder:\\n\\nC:\\\\\\\\Windows\\\\\\\\System32\\\\\\\\config\\\\\\\\systemprofile\\\\\\\\.aws\\\\\\\\\\n\\nC:\\\\\\\\Windows\\\\\\\\System32\\\\\\\\config\\\\\\\\systemprofile\\\\\\\\AppData\\\\\\\\Local\\\\\\\\AWSToolkit\\\\\\\\RegisteredAccounts.json\\n\\nFor your User Profile:\\n\\n%USERPROFILE%\\\\\\\\.aws\\\\\\\\\\n\\n%USERPROFILE%\\\\\\\\AppData\\\\\\\\Local\\\\\\\\AWSToolkit\\\\\\\\RegisteredAccounts.json\\n\\nTo confirm that you deleted the credentials, reboot your server and then test the patch again.\\n\\n### Troubleshoot instances that can't search for Windows updates\\n\\nThe following error messages show that your instance can't search for Windows updates:\\n\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : Exception Details: An error occurred when attempting to search Windows Update. Error Message: Exception from HRESULT: 0x80240437\\\"\\n*   \\\"Invoke-PatchBaselineOperation : Exception Details: An error occurred when attempting to search Windows Update. Error Message: Exception from HRESULT: 0x80072EE2\\\"\\n\\nIf you can't search for Windows updates then you must reset your Windows update components. You also can't search for Windows updates when you can't connect to the Windows Update Catalog or Windows Server Update Services (WSUS).\\n\\nTo resolve these errors, reset your Windows update components and verify that your instance connects to the Windows Update Catalog or WSUS. Complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Determine whether the instance connects through a proxy or with WSUS to the Microsoft patch source.\\n2. Check that you can search for Windows Updates in your instance.\\n3. If your instance uses a WSUS connection, then run the following commands to check your WSUS configuration:.  \\n    To check the group policy, run the following command:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    gpresult /H %USERPROFILE%\\\\Desktop\\\\report.html\\n    ```\\n    \\n4. To check the for registry keys, run the following commands:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\\\Software\\\\Policies\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\WindowsUpdate\\\\AU' | Select-Object AUOptions, NoAutoUpdate, UseWUServer -and- Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\\\\Software\\\\Policies\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\WindowsUpdate' | Select-Object DisableWindowsUpdateAccess, WUServer, WUStatusServer\\n    ```\\n    \\n5. If your WSUS configuration isn't correct, then use a group policy or registry keys to configure WSUS servers.\\n6. If your instance uses a proxy configuration, then check the proxy configuration. For detailed proxy troubleshooting steps, see [Configure SSM Agent to use a proxy for Windows Server instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/configure-proxy-ssm-agent-windows.html).  \\n    **Note:** If you configure your proxy settings for only SSM Agent, then Patch manager doesn't correctly function. To correctly configure system-wide proxy settings, run the following command:\\n    ```plaintext\\n    netsh winhttp set proxy proxy-server=\\\"hostname:port\\\" bypass-list=\\\"169.254.169.254\\\"\\n    ```\\n    \\n7. Reset your Windows Update components and then patch your instance again. For instructions, see [Windows Update - additional resources](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/installing-updates-features-roles/additional-resources-for-windows-update) on the Microsoft website.\\n8. If you receive a \\\"0x80072EE2\\\" error, then verify that your server has access to the following URLs:  \\n    http://windowsupdate.microsoft.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.windowsupdate.microsoft.com  \\n    https://update.microsoft.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.update.microsoft.com  \\n    https://windowsupdate.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.windowsupdate.com  \\n    https://download.windowsupdate.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.download.windowsupdate.com  \\n    https://download.microsoft.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.download.windowsupdate.com  \\n    https://wustat.windows.com  \\n    https://\\\\*.wustat.windows.com  \\n    https://ntservicepack.microsoft.com\\n\\nIf you still can't search for Windows updates, then review your Windows update logs for \\\"HResults\\\" errors. Then, troubleshoot your error based on the error code that you see.\\n\\n**Note:** If you use Windows Server versions 2016 and newer, then before you review your logs run the Get-WindowsUpdateLog PowerShell command. For more information, see [Get-WindowsUpdateLog](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/windowsupdate/get-windowsupdatelog?view=windowsserver2025-ps&viewFallbackFrom=win10-ps) on the Microsoft website.\\n\\nReview your Windows Update logs at the following location:\\n\\n%windir%/WindowsUpdate.log\\n\\nFor Windows Server managed nodes, also review the AWS-RunPatchBaseline logs at the following location:\\n\\n%PROGRAMDATA%\\\\\\\\Amazon\\\\\\\\PatchBaselineOperations\\\\\\\\Logs\\n\\n### Troubleshoot updates that fail to install\\n\\nTo resolve failed installations for downloaded updates, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. Review the patch installation logs at **C:\\\\\\\\Windows\\\\\\\\Logs\\\\\\\\CBS** and match the timestamp of the command that's running. Then, review the logs for error messages.\\n2. If the patch requires a reboot, then reboot your instance.\\n3. If the patch doesn't install after you reboot your instance, then [take a screenshot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-console.html#instance-console-screenshot) and then review the message on the login screen.  \\n    **Note:** If you see the following message on the boot screen, then don't reboot your instance:  \\n    \\\"We couldn't complete the updates. Undoing changes. Don't turn off your computer\\\"\\n4. In the Component-Based Servicing (CBS) log file, find the **HResult** code. Then, search for the code on the [Windows Update common errors and mitigation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-client/deployment/common-windows-update-errors) documentation o\",\"total_length\":10708,\"start_index\":0,\"end_index\":10000,\"truncated\":true,\"redirected_url\":null,\"error_code\":null}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

To maximize their compatibility it uses the .NET Framework 3.5 version of the SDK. Version 3.3.270.0 of the AWSPowerShell module is built with the newer version of AWSSDK.Core, which has this fix to force new TLS protocols when available\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/developer/upgrade-aws-sdk-for-net-for-latest-tls-protocols/\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Prerequisites to create Windows VSS based EBS snapshots\",\"context\":\"## System requirements\\n\\n**Install the Systems Manager Agent**\\n: VSS is orchestrated by the Systems Manager Agent using PowerShell. Ensure that you have\\n installed SSM Agent version `3.0.502.0` or later on your EC2 instance. If\\n you are already using an older version of the SSM Agent, update it using Run Command.\\n For more information, see Setting up Systems Manager for Amazon EC2 instances and Working with\\n SSM Agent on Amazon EC2 instances for Windows Server in the\\n *AWS Systems Manager User Guide*.\\n\\n**Amazon EC2 Windows instance requirements**\\n: VSS based EBS snapshots are supported for instances running\\n Windows Server 2016 and later.\\n\\n**.NET Framework version**\\n: The `AwsVssComponents` package requires .NET Framework version `4.6`\\n or later. Windows operating system versions prior to Windows Server 2016 default to an\\n earlier version of the .NET Framework. If your instance uses an earlier version of the\\n .NET Framework, you must install version `4.6` or later using Windows Update.\\n\\n**AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell version**\\n: Ensure that your instance is running AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell version `3.3.48.0` or later.\\n To check your version, run the following command in the PowerShell terminal on the\\n instance.\\n\\n ```\\n C:\\\\> Get-AWSPowerShellVersion\\n ```\\n\\n If you need to update AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell on your instance, see Installing the AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell in the *AWS Tools for PowerShell User Guide*.\\n\\n**Windows PowerShell version**\\n: Ensure that your instance is running Windows PowerShell major version `3`,\\n `4`, or `5`. To check your version, run the following command\\n in a PowerShell terminal on the instance.\\n\\n ```\\n C:\\\\> $PSVersionTable.PSVersion\\n ```\\n\\n**PowerShell language mode**\\n: Ensure that your instance has the PowerShell language mode set to `FullLanguage`.\\n For more information, see about_Language_Modes in the Microsoft documentation\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/application-consistent-snapshots-prereqs.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Enforcing a minimum TLS version in the AWS SDK for .NET\",\"context\":\"## AWS Tools for PowerShell\\n\\nAWS Tools for PowerShell use the AWS SDK for .NET for all calls to AWS services.\\nThe behavior of your environment depends on the version of Windows PowerShell you're running, as\\nfollows.\\n\\n**Windows PowerShell 2.0 through 5.x**\\n\\nWindows PowerShell 2.0 through 5.x run on .NET Framework. You can verify which .NET runtime (2.0 or\\n4.0) is being used by PowerShell by using the following command.\\n\\n```\\n$PSVersionTable.CLRVersion\\n```\\n\\n* When using .NET Runtime 2.0, follow the instructions provided earlier regarding the AWS SDK for .NET\\n and .NET Framework 3.5.\\n\\n **Warning:**\\n\\n Starting August 15th, 2024, the AWS SDK for .NET will end support for .NET Framework 3.5 and will change\\n the minimum .NET Framework version to 4.7.2. For more information, see the blog post Important changes coming for .NET Framework 3.5 and 4.5 targets of the AWS SDK for .NET.\\n* When using .NET Runtime 4.0, follow the instructions provided earlier regarding the AWS SDK for .NET\\n and .NET Framework 4+.\\n\\n**Windows PowerShell 6.0**\\n\\nWindows PowerShell 6.0 and newer run on .NET Core. You can verify which version of .NET Core is\\nbeing used by running the following command.\\n\\n```\\n[System.Reflection.Assembly]::GetEntryAssembly().GetCustomAttributes([System.Runtime.Versioning.TargetFrameworkAttribute], $true).FrameworkName\\n```\\n\\nFollow the instructions provided earlier regarding the AWS SDK for .NET and the relevant version of .NET\\nCore\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-net/v3/developer-guide/enforcing-tls.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Running Verify Aws Claim"}

{"id": "3bf062e2-f5b0-41c4-9b01-fc78c4d81883", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I don't have confirmed AWS documentation that covers this exact assembly-load error, so I'll be upfront: this isn't one of the documented failure modes in AWS's own patching troubleshooting guide (which covers S3 connectivity, invalid tokens, WSUS/Windows Update search failures, and failed installs — none of which match what you're seeing). What I can tell you comes from well-established .NET/PowerShell behavior that explains this specific error.

**What's actually going on**

`AWS-RunPatchBaseline` on Windows runs as a PowerShell module (`AWSPowerShell` / the Patch Baseline module) that depends on `AWSSDK.Core.dll`. The error:

```
Could not load type 'Amazon.Runtime.Internal.InvokeOptions' from assembly 'AWSSDK.Core'
```

is a classic **.NET assembly version mismatch** — the runtime successfully resolved *an* `AWSSDK.Core.dll`, but it's the wrong version: one that predates (or postdates) the type the loaded PowerShell module code expects. This happens, not because Windows itself is broken (which is why manual OS patching works fine — that path never touches these assemblies), but because something on disk put a stale or conflicting `AWSSDK.Core.dll` where the .NET assembly resolver finds it before the correct one. Common root causes:

1. **A stale AWS Tools for PowerShell / AWSSDK.Core.dll in the Global Assembly Cache (GAC) or a module path** that's older than what the current SSM Agent / patch baseline module expects, and it's getting loaded instead of the correct version.
2. **A corrupted or partial SSM Agent install/update** that left mismatched DLL versions in `C:\Program Files\Amazon\SSM\` or the PatchBaselineOperations module folder.
3. **A manually installed AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell module** (via a different path than SSM Agent's bundled copy) that's shadowing the correct assembly.

**How to fix it**

1. Check the SSM Agent version — update to the latest if not current:
   ```powershell
   Get-Item "C:\Program Files\Amazon\SSM\amazon-ssm-agent.exe" | Select VersionInfo
   ```
   If outdated, update it via Run Command (`AWS-UpdateSSMAgent`) or reinstall the MSI manually.

2. **Reinstall/repair the SSM Agent** entirely — this is the most reliable fix since it refreshes the bundled AWSSDK.Core.dll that ships alongside the agent and the PatchBaselineOperations module:
   - Stop the `AmazonSSMAgent` service
   - Uninstall it via Programs and Features (or `msiexec /x`)
   - Download and reinstall the latest SSM Agent MSI for Windows
   - Restart the service

3. **Check for a conflicting AWSSDK.Core.dll in the GAC**:
   ```powershell
   [System.Reflection.Assembly]::LoadWithPartialName("AWSSDK.Core").Location
   ```
   If this resolves to a path outside the SSM Agent's own folders (e.g., an old AWS Tools for PowerShell install under `Program Files\WindowsPowerShell\Modules\AWSPowerShell`), that's likely your culprit — uninstall/update that separate module.

4. After reinstalling, review `%PROGRAMDATA%\Amazon\PatchBaselineOperations\Logs` and the SSM Agent logs at `C:\ProgramData\Amazon\SSM\Logs\amazon-ssm-agent.log` to confirm the module now loads correctly.

Given the specificity of this error and that it's not in AWS's published troubleshooting doc, I'd also recommend opening an AWS Support case if the reinstall doesn't resolve it — want me to file one for you?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
